name: pH
question: How acidic or basic is it? 7 is neutral; every step down is ten times more acidic.

items.name: Battery acid
items.fact: Car battery acid is sulfuric acid, strong enough to burn skin.

items.name: Gastric acid
items.fact: Your stomach lining replaces itself every few days to survive its own acid.

items.name: Vinegar
items.fact: Vinegar is mostly water with about 5–8% acetic acid.

items.name: Orange juice
items.fact: Orange juice is acidic enough to soften tooth enamel.

items.name: Human skin
items.fact: Skin's slightly acidic surface is sometimes called the 'acid mantle'.

items.name: Black coffee
items.fact: Dark roasts are usually slightly less acidic than light roasts.

items.name: Urine
items.fact: Urine pH swings with diet: lots of meat makes it more acidic.

items.name: Milk
items.fact: Milk turns sour as bacteria make lactic acid and the pH drops.

items.name: Pure water
items.fact: Pure water is neutral, but rainwater is slightly acidic from dissolved CO₂.

items.name: Human blood
items.fact: Blood pH outside about 7.35–7.45 is a medical emergency.

items.name: Seawater
items.fact: The ocean surface has become measurably more acidic since 1950.

items.name: Household ammonia
items.fact: Never mix ammonia with bleach: together they release toxic gas.

items.name: Bleach
items.fact: Household bleach is a dilute solution of sodium hypochlorite.

items.name: Lye (drain cleaner)
items.fact: Lye has been used for centuries to make soap.
